question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the institutional structure of rural banking?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Moneylenders.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Today's institutional** framework for rural banking** comprises of a number of **multi-agency entities**, including

 
 
• commercial banks,
 
• Regional Rural Banks,
 
• co-operatives, and
 
• land development banks.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups** (SHGs) have recently appeared to close the gap in the established credit system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional rural banks:**

 
 
• **In 1975**, the Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were founded.
 
• It was founded in accordance with the terms of the** 1976 Regional Rural Banks Act **and the** Ordinance published** on **September 26, 1975.**
 
• RRBs are **financial organization**s that guarantee **sufficient credit for rural industries like agriculture.**
 
 
 
• **Commercial banks:**
 
 
• A commercial bank is a type of financial organization that offers its clients services including** loans, CDs, savings accounts, overdraft protection, etc.**
 
 
 
• **Cooperative banks:**
 
 
• A co-operative bank is a **diminutive financial institution** whose owners and clients are its members.
 
• They are registered under the** States Cooperative Societies Act **and are governed by the** Reserve Bank of India (RBI).**
 
 
 
• **Land development banks:**
 
 
• The LDB's primary goals are to **advance agricultural development** and productivity as well as land use.
 
• The LDB provides long-term finance to **members directly through its branches.**
